title: The application shell preseeds the polite and assertive live-region wrappers on every declared route before any notification fires
description: Every route the applying project declares under its navigation model renders with the two live-region wrappers already present in the DOM at page load: a `[aria-live="polite"]` wrapper for informational messages and a `[role="alert"]` wrapper for assertive alerts. Both wrappers exist and are empty before any notification fires; a wrapper inserted lazily after the first event is a defect that produces a screen-reader miss per the Sara Soueidan normative guidance on ARIA live regions. The wrappers carry stable `data-live-region="polite"` and `data-live-region="assertive"` attributes so the pack can enumerate them by data-id (not by role attribute alone, per the T-3 gate discipline).
rationale: The WAI-ARIA 1.2 live-regions normative contract requires the container to exist in the DOM before content is inserted; a wrapper inserted at the same tick as the content races the screen-reader announcement pass and the message is silently lost. Preseeding the two wrappers on every route is the runtime discipline that turns the WCAG 4.1.3 status-message clause from a design intent into a runtime-observable check the probe pack can drive.
